A RESOLUTION DECLARING THE TREUTLEN COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS’ INTENT TO REQUEST LOCAL LEGISLATION TO AMEND THE QUALIFYING PROCESS OF LOCAL CANDIDATES SO AS TO ABOLISH PARTISAN QUALIFYING AND TO HAVE LOCAL CANDIDATES QUALIFY AS NON-PARTISAN, WITHOUT POLITICAL PARTY AFFILIATION.

On this day, the 9't day of September, 2010, the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners have met for the purpose of discussing and passing a resolution, declaring its intent to request local legislation from its Georgia State Senator and Representative, so as to amend the qualifying process and requirements of local candidates for elected public office, so that local candidates shall not qualify in partisan primaries, but qualify as non-partisan candidates, without a political party affiliation.

WHEREAS, the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners believes that it is in the best interests of Treutlen County and its citizens to amend the qualifying process of local candidates; and

WHEREAS, the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners contend that the partisan primary process regarding local candidates seeking to qualify for local elections creates unnecessary delay and expense to the citizens of Treutlen

County; and

WHEREAS, the duties and demands of local elected officials are not dependent upon the policies, platforms, or financial support of national political parties; and

WHEREAS, the abolishment of partisan primaries of local candidates would spare the citizens of Treutlen County expense and streamline the local election process; and

WHEREAS, the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners believe that it is prudent and wise to seek local legislation to amend the qualifying of candidates for local races so as to abolish partisan primaries and have all candidates for local office to run as non-partisan candidates, without a political party affiliation;

THEREFORE, upon a motion and second by the Treutlen County Commissioners, such resolution was passed unanimously, and the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners declares and issues the following Resolution:

BE IT RESOLVED, that the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners of Treutlen County, Georgia hereby request local legislation from its Georgia State Senator and Representative, so as to amend the qualifying process and requirements of local candidates for elected public office, so that local candidates shall not qualify in partisan primaries, but qualify as non-partisan candidates, without a political party affiliation.

Severability Clause: If any part or portion of this resolution shall be ruled invalid, unconstitutional, or otherwise unlawful, the remaining body of the resolution shall remain in full force and effect.

Repealer Clause: This resolution effectively and immediately replaces and otherwise repeals any prior conflicting ordinance or resolution of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners.

Effective Date: This resolution shall become _ effective immediately, but shall not invalidate any ongoing project by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners.

This the 9 day of September, 2010.

Re: Resolution by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners, requesting local legislation to have county elected officials run as non-partisan candidates

Dear Gentlemen,

There has been a request by some Treutlen County citizens to amend the qualifying process of local candidates in Treutlen County, so as to abolish partisan qualifying and have all locally elected officials qualify as non-partisan candidates, so as to run only in the general election. Many other counties have previously made this change and I believe that Treutlen County may be one the few counties in this immediate area that still has its local candidates qualify with a political party affiliation.

Upon consideration of the issue the Treutlen County Board of Commnissioners recently passed a Resolution, requesting the introduction of local legislation to amend the qualifying process, so as to provide for non-partisan local elections.

Enclosed herein you will find a copy of the Board’s Resolution for you to consider. The Treutlen County Board of Commissioners would appreciate each of you sponsoring local legislation to modify the qualification process in Treutlen County, Georgia.
